compare_blocks.body:
Boundary of use: the three scenes below are fictional, used only to set two kinds of evidence and two outward stances side by side. They correspond to no real project, organisation or person, and they are not a basis for dividing work. Work is assigned by post, qualification and project procedure, never by type. Anything touching structure, fire safety or electrical systems starts with the original design records, verification by qualified professionals and approval under the applicable procedure; nothing is touched before that.

### INFJ and ISTP: who writes the constraint and who writes the dimension

(Fictional scene) A temporary change note normally carries two kinds of content. One is checkable quantity: what changed, the dimensions and elevations, where the supports sit. The other is constraint: the access panel must not be sealed, the fall must not go below the original design, a named party must be notified before acceptance. Both matter, and missing either invites rework.

In this fictional project the two may each lean toward one kind: the one collecting quantities writes them in detail, the one watching ramifications writes them in full. But who writes which part should follow post and qualification — drawing and checking belong to people with the relevant credentials, and sign-off follows the project's procedure. The consequences of a wrong dimension or a missing constraint are traced through the post responsibilities and review stages in the project, not attached to a type.

A workable check: leave three lines on the back of each change note — what changed, which later work is affected, who signed. Look at the three lines side by side at month end; if the impact line is usually empty, a stage is missing from the process. These three lines verify closure, not anyone's preference.

### INFJ and ISTP: a neighbour asks about taking out a wall

A neighbour has bought a flat and wants to remove the wall between the living room and the second bedroom, and asks both for an opinion. This is also fictional, and it involves structural safety, which experience cannot settle.

The two may care about different things first: one more often asks how you want to live in the flat, and whether what is missing is a larger living room or a study with a door that closes; the other more often asks what this wall is on the original drawing, and whether the flats above and below are the same. Both questions need asking, but neither may become a yes given before verification.

The boundary has to be explicit: whether a wall is load-bearing and whether it can come out cannot be decided by thickness or by tapping it. What works is checking the original design drawings and archived structural records, having a qualified structural engineer verify on site, and filing the renovation and alteration permits required locally. Nothing is demolished before that, and no verbal "it should be fine" is offered. This has nothing to do with type; it holds for both.

One counterexample: the one who checks structure first will also ask whether the heating will still cope in winter; the one who asks about daily life first will also go and find the building's structural records before giving any advice.

### INFJ and ISTP: reviewing a request for additional payment

After the change, the crew submits an extra-cost claim. In this fictional scene the two may check different things first: one checks labour and material — how many extra metres of pipe, how many supports, how many labour hours, and what that comes to at market rates; the other looks at how the contract treats this money and why the claim arrives only now. Both need checking.

In this fictional review, put the quantities and relevant contract terms side by side so the approver can see what is documented and what still needs checking. The team can review both without inferring anyone’s motives.

Who may confirm the increment and who signs the supplementary agreement follows the contract terms and project authority, not type.
compare_blocks.title: Illustrative scenarios

compare_blocks.body:
Reading INFJ as overthinking and unable to decide is a common error. The hesitation may not be about whether to change anything but about who is affected once it changes; once the impact is spelled out, the signature may come quickly. That is a conditional description, not a rule.

Reading ISTP as seeing only the immediate is also inaccurate. The way consequences get considered may lean toward how this section of pipe will fail later and which joint goes first, rather than what the whole thing means. Both are long-range; the language differs.

The third misread is quietness. The shared I says attention turns inward more often, not how much anyone speaks. Saying little may come from preference, from the setting, from seniority, or from there being nothing that needs saying at that moment. Judging type by how much someone talks in a meeting will almost certainly fail — and it is equally wrong to infer who is better suited to technical work or to coordination.

The fourth misread treats "the same four function names" as evidence that the two are alike. Shared names mean shared material; the difference is the seating. In the other direction, three differing letters do not mean the two have no common language.

body: In the same meeting, either person might listen quietly or speak at length about a subject they know. Role, familiarity and the setting help explain how much someone says.
Both types share a preference for directing attention and energy inward. Introversion does not measure social skill, talkativeness or assertiveness.

S/N concerns the information someone tends to emphasize: concrete observations and relevant experience, or patterns and possibilities. T/F concerns the criteria used to weigh a decision. J/P concerns the preference for establishing an arrangement or keeping options open in the outer world. Experience, deadlines and new information can affect how quickly either person acts.
The letters and the function order answer different questions. The letters describe preferences. Type dynamics uses those letters to explain which processes are dominant and auxiliary.
### INFJ and ISTP: one pipe clash, two kinds of evidence

Picture a project site: a fire-service pipe and a newly added cable tray clash at the same elevation, and the crew needs an answer today. This is a fictional scene used to set two kinds of evidence side by side, not an observation of a real project or real people.

In this fictional review, two people have the same drawings, site measurements and authority. For S/N, one question is what the measured clearance shows, and another is whether the clash points to a recurring layout problem. For T/F, one question is whether a proposed decision meets the same criteria used elsewhere, and another is how that decision would affect people responsible for using or maintaining the space. Either person can ask each question.

Measurements establish the current conditions. Looking at related drawings may show where the same problem could recur. Both checks can inform the review, and the project procedure determines who can perform or approve them.
Either person may flag a downstream effect or ask someone qualified to verify a measurement. Who asks first depends on role, training and the information at hand.

Whether a change is properly closed can be checked against three items: the change note is signed, the as-built drawing is updated, and later work is not blocked by this modification. These three verify the process only and are not used to type anyone; who draws, who checks and who signs follows post, qualification and project procedure.

In the four-function notation used here, INFJ is Ni–Fe–Ti–Se and ISTP is Ti–Se–Ni–Fe. The four names are identical and the order rotates by two seats: INFJ's first and second positions become ISTP's third and fourth, and the reverse. It is a rotation, not a reversal.

The letters identify the preferred side of each pair. Type dynamics arranges the processes in a theoretical order. A position in the stack does not tell you which process a person will use first in a specific situation.
Both stacks contain the perceiving pair Ni and Se and the judging pair Fe and Ti. INFJ leads with Ni, a perceiving process. ISTP leads with Ti, a judging process.

body: The table puts both into the same temporary change: one clash, one batch of information, the same programme and approval route. Both types can use both approaches; the rows describe evidence likely to be consulted first, not the only thing anyone does, and they are not six personality dimensions.

Align the conditions before reading: if one is the site lead and the other was called over to take a look, role will swamp both columns. If one happens to be holding the tape and the drawings, the columns may invert.

| The same scene (one clash, one batch of information, the same deadline) | INFJ: evidence likely to be consulted first | ISTP: evidence likely to be consulted first | What this row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The pipe and the tray clash, with the same drawings and records in hand | Whether records from different parts of the building show the same clash, and which connections are still unverified | Elevations, clearances and the exact point of clash, with records that can be traced back | S/N: pattern against specific fact; both should refer the decision to qualified staff within their authority |

body: Boundary of use: the three scenes below are fictional, used only to set two kinds of evidence and two outward stances side by side. They correspond to no real project, organisation or person, and they are not a basis for dividing work. Work is assigned by post, qualification and project procedure, never by type. Anything touching structure, fire safety or electrical systems starts with the original design records, verification by qualified professionals and approval under the applicable procedure; nothing is touched before that.
### INFJ and ISTP: who writes the constraint and who writes the dimension

(Fictional scene) A temporary change note normally carries two kinds of content. One is checkable quantity: what changed, the dimensions and elevations, where the supports sit. The other is constraint: the access panel must not be sealed, the fall must not go below the original design, a named party must be notified before acceptance. Both matter, and missing either invites rework.

In this fictional project the two may each lean toward one kind: the one collecting quantities writes them in detail, the one watching ramifications writes them in full. But who writes which part should follow post and qualification — drawing and checking belong to people with the relevant credentials, and sign-off follows the project's procedure. The consequences of a wrong dimension or a missing constraint are traced through the post responsibilities and review stages in the project, not attached to a type.

A workable check: leave three lines on the back of each change note — what changed, which later work is affected, who signed. Look at the three lines side by side at month end; if the impact line is usually empty, a stage is missing from the process. These three lines verify closure, not anyone's preference.
### INFJ and ISTP: a neighbour asks about taking out a wall

A neighbour has bought a flat and wants to remove the wall between the living room and the second bedroom, and asks both for an opinion. This is also fictional, and it involves structural safety, which experience cannot settle.

The two may care about different things first: one more often asks how you want to live in the flat, and whether what is missing is a larger living room or a study with a door that closes; the other more often asks what this wall is on the original drawing, and whether the flats above and below are the same. Both questions need asking, but neither may become a yes given before verification.

The boundary has to be explicit: whether a wall is load-bearing and whether it can come out cannot be decided by thickness or by tapping it. What works is checking the original design drawings and archived structural records, having a qualified structural engineer verify on site, and filing the renovation and alteration permits required locally. Nothing is demolished before that, and no verbal "it should be fine" is offered. This has nothing to do with type; it holds for both.

One counterexample: the one who checks structure first will also ask whether the heating will still cope in winter; the one who asks about daily life first will also go and find the building's structural records before giving any advice.
### INFJ and ISTP: reviewing a request for additional payment

After the change, the crew submits an extra-cost claim. In this fictional scene the two may check different things first: one checks labour and material — how many extra metres of pipe, how many supports, how many labour hours, and what that comes to at market rates; the other looks at how the contract treats this money and why the claim arrives only now. Both need checking.

In this fictional review, put the quantities and relevant contract terms side by side so the approver can see what is documented and what still needs checking. The team can review both without inferring anyone’s motives.
Who may confirm the increment and who signs the supplementary agreement follows the contract terms and project authority, not type.

body: Reading INFJ as overthinking and unable to decide is a common error. The hesitation may not be about whether to change anything but about who is affected once it changes; once the impact is spelled out, the signature may come quickly. That is a conditional description, not a rule.

Reading ISTP as seeing only the immediate is also inaccurate. The way consequences get considered may lean toward how this section of pipe will fail later and which joint goes first, rather than what the whole thing means. Both are long-range; the language differs.

The third misread is quietness. The shared I says attention turns inward more often, not how much anyone speaks. Saying little may come from preference, from the setting, from seniority, or from there being nothing that needs saying at that moment. Judging type by how much someone talks in a meeting will almost certainly fail — and it is equally wrong to infer who is better suited to technical work or to coordination.

The fourth misread treats "the same four function names" as evidence that the two are alike. Shared names mean shared material; the difference is the seating. In the other direction, three differing letters do not mean the two have no common language.

The table puts both into the same temporary change: one clash, one batch of information, the same programme and approval route. Both types can use both approaches; the rows describe evidence likely to be consulted first, not the only thing anyone does, and they are not six personality dimensions.

Align the conditions before reading: if one is the site lead and the other was called over to take a look, role will swamp both columns. If one happens to be holding the tape and the drawings, the columns may invert.

| The same scene (one clash, one batch of information, the same deadline) | INFJ: evidence likely to be consulted first | ISTP: evidence likely to be consulted first | What this row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The pipe and the tray clash, with the same drawings and records in hand | Whether records from different parts of the building show the same clash, and which connections are still unverified | Elevations, clearances and the exact point of clash, with records that can be traced back | S/N: pattern against specific fact; both should refer the decision to qualified staff within their authority |
| Judging whether a fix holds | Who maintains it afterwards, and how a failure would be explained | Whether the same fix holds consistently under the same conditions, and whether a solution needs less demolition | Standard of judgement, leaning T/F |
| How to coordinate the review while the measurements are still being verified | Agree on a provisional review plan and a time to revisit it | Keep two workable review plans open until the same measurements are verified | Approach to outward arrangements: J/P |
| What evidence to include in the change note | Flag a possible pattern across the drawings and identify which other locations need checking | Record the measured clearance and cite the drawing for this location | Information gathering: S/N |
| Both review the same verified quantities and contract terms for an extra-cost claim | Weigh how the options allowed by the same contract affect the crew and those who depend on the work | Apply the same eligibility and documentation criteria used for comparable claims | Standard of judgement, leaning T/F |
| How to prepare for another clash with the same approval requirements | Agree on a provisional review process that the team can revisit | Keep several workable review processes available for the next situation | Approach to outward arrangements: J/P |

None of these rows is a scale of ability. Someone with years on site will usually collect data out of professional habit; someone facing this for the first time may only stand and watch. The same person will also change approach depending on duty, experience and whether someone else has already filled the information gaps, so these rows cannot be used to classify anyone.
sections.title: INFJ and ISTP in one minute

sections.body_md:
Boundary of use: the three scenes below are fictional, used only to set two kinds of evidence and two outward stances side by side. They correspond to no real project, organisation or person, and they are not a basis for dividing work. Work is assigned by post, qualification and project procedure, never by type. Anything touching structure, fire safety or electrical systems starts with the original design records, verification by qualified professionals and approval under the applicable procedure; nothing is touched before that.

### INFJ and ISTP: who writes the constraint and who writes the dimension

(Fictional scene) A temporary change note normally carries two kinds of content. One is checkable quantity: what changed, the dimensions and elevations, where the supports sit. The other is constraint: the access panel must not be sealed, the fall must not go below the original design, a named party must be notified before acceptance. Both matter, and missing either invites rework.

In this fictional project the two may each lean toward one kind: the one collecting quantities writes them in detail, the one watching ramifications writes them in full. But who writes which part should follow post and qualification — drawing and checking belong to people with the relevant credentials, and sign-off follows the project's procedure. The consequences of a wrong dimension or a missing constraint are traced through the post responsibilities and review stages in the project, not attached to a type.

A workable check: leave three lines on the back of each change note — what changed, which later work is affected, who signed. Look at the three lines side by side at month end; if the impact line is usually empty, a stage is missing from the process. These three lines verify closure, not anyone's preference.

### INFJ and ISTP: a neighbour asks about taking out a wall

A neighbour has bought a flat and wants to remove the wall between the living room and the second bedroom, and asks both for an opinion. This is also fictional, and it involves structural safety, which experience cannot settle.

The two may care about different things first: one more often asks how you want to live in the flat, and whether what is missing is a larger living room or a study with a door that closes; the other more often asks what this wall is on the original drawing, and whether the flats above and below are the same. Both questions need asking, but neither may become a yes given before verification.

The boundary has to be explicit: whether a wall is load-bearing and whether it can come out cannot be decided by thickness or by tapping it. What works is checking the original design drawings and archived structural records, having a qualified structural engineer verify on site, and filing the renovation and alteration permits required locally. Nothing is demolished before that, and no verbal "it should be fine" is offered. This has nothing to do with type; it holds for both.

One counterexample: the one who checks structure first will also ask whether the heating will still cope in winter; the one who asks about daily life first will also go and find the building's structural records before giving any advice.

### INFJ and ISTP: reviewing a request for additional payment

After the change, the crew submits an extra-cost claim. In this fictional scene the two may check different things first: one checks labour and material — how many extra metres of pipe, how many supports, how many labour hours, and what that comes to at market rates; the other looks at how the contract treats this money and why the claim arrives only now. Both need checking.

In this fictional review, put the quantities and relevant contract terms side by side so the approver can see what is documented and what still needs checking. The team can review both without inferring anyone’s motives.

Who may confirm the increment and who signs the supplementary agreement follows the contract terms and project authority, not type.
sections.title: INFJ and ISTP at work and in relationships

sections.body_md:
Reading INFJ as overthinking and unable to decide is a common error. The hesitation may not be about whether to change anything but about who is affected once it changes; once the impact is spelled out, the signature may come quickly. That is a conditional description, not a rule.

Reading ISTP as seeing only the immediate is also inaccurate. The way consequences get considered may lean toward how this section of pipe will fail later and which joint goes first, rather than what the whole thing means. Both are long-range; the language differs.

The third misread is quietness. The shared I says attention turns inward more often, not how much anyone speaks. Saying little may come from preference, from the setting, from seniority, or from there being nothing that needs saying at that moment. Judging type by how much someone talks in a meeting will almost certainly fail — and it is equally wrong to infer who is better suited to technical work or to coordination.

The fourth misread treats "the same four function names" as evidence that the two are alike. Shared names mean shared material; the difference is the seating. In the other direction, three differing letters do not mean the two have no common language.
sections.title: INFJ and ISTP: avoiding misreads

sections.body_md:
If the results differ, check the questionnaire, language and scoring guidance. Then consider how your responsibilities may have shaped the examples you had in mind. Reflect on several situations with similar constraints where you had room to choose.

Turn the practice into notes rather than a verdict. Pick a few recent temporary changes and write three lines for each: what information was in hand, what the trade-off rested on, and which steps were required by post or procedure. Read the three lines afterwards: do you more often cite checkable fact or downstream direction; a consistent standard or the people and responsibilities involved; an arrangement fixed first or options kept open.

It is normal for both approaches to appear across a few cases, which shows both are within reach; it does not mean someone is "near the boundary" and does not mean the answers were wrong. Keep such notes for reflection — they are not scored, do not decide a type, and a handful of cases cannot replace the interpretation of an assessment result.
sections.title: INFJ and ISTP: how to keep observing

items.answer:
Because introversion describes only the direction of attention and energy; the other three preferences each describe a different aspect and have nothing to do with being introverted.

S/N governs material: comparable fact and experience, or connections and possibility noticed sooner. T/F governs the standard of judgement: whether a rule applies consistently, or what it means for people. J/P governs the outward stance: an arrangement formed first, or options kept open. INFJ takes N, F and J; ISTP takes S, T and P. All three differ at once, so although the four function names match, the seating is entirely rearranged.
items.question: Both are introverted — why are three letters still different?

items.answer:
The model gives different roles to the four processes: Ni and Fe are dominant and auxiliary for INFJ, while Ti and Se are dominant and auxiliary for ISTP.

In the writing used here, INFJ is Ni–Fe–Ti–Se and ISTP is Ti–Se–Ni–Fe, rotated by two seats so that the first two and last two swap. Position describes emphasis only. It does not predict who does what first, and it does not say whether the two work well together, who is drawn to whom, or who suits which job — those depend far more on the individuals, their duties and their shared experience.
items.question: The four function names are identical — why do the two read so differently?

items.answer:
Yes, especially when a change affects acceptance or later use.

The way it gets considered may be more concrete: whether the client will reject it, who will repair this pipe later, who bears the cost of rework. Both types can put the human factor early or late; the difference is which kind of evidence gets cited more, and sequence alone is not a test — duty and experience push behaviour toward the other side as well.
items.question: Does an ISTP also consider what the client will think?

items.answer:
Either type can assess feasibility and consider downstream effects. A complete change note needs both.

Feasibility covers whether it can be done, at what cost, and what new problems it creates; ramifications cover who is affected, how it will be accounted for later, and whether notice must be given in advance. Feasibility alone tends to produce a change that is overturned after completion; ramifications alone tends to produce an afternoon of discussion with no work started. This is not a division of labour by type: who can fill which part depends on post, qualification and the information at hand, and on who is authorised on the project.
items.question: In a temporary site change, what does each contribute?

items.answer:
That silence is not agreement.

Both may be used to thinking before speaking, and the gap in between is easily read by the other as consent or coldness. A workable agreement sets a time limit on silence: if there is no reply within half a day, ask directly whether the thinking is unfinished or the answer is no. That is a communication agreement, useful to both types and unrelated to type — and it should not be turned around to infer someone's preference from their silence.
items.question: What matters most to say in advance when the two live or work together?

items.answer:
Check the tool, language version and scoring definition used in each sitting, rather than working backwards from the four-letter result to a score.

If the tool reports comparable sub-measures, check whether S/N, T/F and J/P each sit near their own classification threshold — these two results differ on all three, so explaining the gap by one or two of them will not work. Without sub-scores or scoring notes, do not infer "close to the boundary" and do not prescribe a retest interval; record the situations you were referring to and the items you hesitated over, as material for reflection.

Framework sources: preference definitions follow the [Myers-Briggs official facts page](https://www.themyersbriggs.com/en-us/support/mbti-facts); the type-dynamics framework follows the [Foundation's note on type dynamics](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-processes/) and the [type dynamics overview](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/). Both are used to understand type dynamics and preference definitions; neither is a behaviour checklist.

Four-position convention on this page: Ni–Fe–Ti–Se for INFJ and Ti–Se–Ni–Fe for ISTP follow a common four-function notation adopted here; sources handle the attitude of the third process differently, and this is not presented as the Foundation's only reading.

Editorial fiction note: the pipe clash, the wall question and the extra-cost claim are all editorial fiction, used to illustrate ways of comparing preferences, and correspond to no real project, organisation or person. Dimensions and support details mentioned are proposals awaiting review, to be implemented only after design verification and formal approval; the wall section is not a basis for any structural judgement.

Scope limits: this page discusses emphasis between preferences, not ability, skill or the order of behaviour. Results are not for ranking ability, hiring screens or predicting relationships, and not for inferring who is better suited to technical work or to coordination. Anything involving structure, fire safety, electrical systems or personal safety starts with the original design records, verification by qualified professionals and approval under the applicable procedure.
